page: Amazon Web Services a1.xlarge is an ARM-based compute instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by first-generation AWS Graviton processors. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores running on 64-bit ARMv8 Cortex-A72 microarchitecture clocked at 2.3 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core and 2 MB of shared L2 cache, lacking an L3 cache. Memory is configured at 8.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators and operates on a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results reflect the limitations of the first-generation Graviton architecture across compute and memory workloads. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 408.0 and a multi-core score of 1245.0, both landing in the bottom tier of measured cloud instances. PassMark CPU testing yielded an overall score of 1618.39, alongside 913.43 for memory and 1263.44 for database operations. Memory bandwidth tests produced 12.56 GB/sec for large un-cached read operations and 6.77 GB/sec for write operations. Network static web throughput measured 1.36 GB/sec, while in-memory Redis SET operations reached 2.13 million operations per second.

Given the modest per-core throughput and absence of local NVMe storage, the a1.xlarge delivers cost-efficient resource provisioning primarily for scale-out architectures designed around native ARM execution. It provides a dedicated core execution environment without CPU stealing or thread contention, making it viable for lightweight web frontends, basic microservices, continuous integration build targets compiling ARM binaries, and non-critical development workloads that do not require intense floating-point or vector performance.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.xlarge is a dedicated ARM64 compute instance featuring 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by first-generation AWS Graviton Cortex-A72 processors clocked at 2.3 GHz. Configured with 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) and running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers a 1:2 compute-to-memory configuration. It includes no bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration, relying on EBS volumes and a 1 Gbps baseline network link. Empirical benchmark measurements show entry-level execution rates across single-core and multi-core evaluations, including a Geekbench multi-core rating of 1245.0 and PassMark CPU score of 1618.39. With support for standard cryptographic extensions like AES, the a1.xlarge is suited for scale-out web applications, ARM software compilation pipelines, light caching layers, and containerized microservices requiring predictable dedicated physical cores without high compute density demands.
